summary: USB-only power puts ADC VDRIVE above its absolute maximum relative to AVCC
description: U1 exports +3V3 while USB powers Seed3 without carrier +5A. U2.23 is tied to +3V3 but U2 AVCC pins 1/37/38/48 are on +5A. Thus VDRIVE=3.3V, AVCC=0V violates the AVCC+0.3V maximum. Different shutdown decay times create a similar sequencing risk. The output permit does not protect supply pins.
recommendation: Resolve ADC supply sequencing and powered-off host signal injection before USB-only use; do not treat the Seed VIN reverse protection as carrier-wide power isolation. Qualify all power-up/down orders.

summary: Target conversion rates exceed stock libDaisy clock and shared DMA capacity
description: Both SPI handles use DMA2_Stream2/3 and one static active-peripheral gate. At target 25MHz, serialized ADC and DAC payloads consume 104.448% of time before any overhead. Default libDaisy further uses PLL2P=25MHz for SPI123, and /2 minimum prescaler gives 12.5MHz SCK: the ADC alone needs 11.52us for a 10.417us sample period.
recommendation: Keep the new backend explicitly pending. Specify and test SPI kernel clocks, DMA ownership and a valid burst schedule. A future 100MHz kernel with ADC /2 and DAC /4 reduces average payload to 76.8%, but requires ADC reads interleaved between DAC words and does not prove timing closure.

summary: Fixed IN1-IN4 inputs have no defined DC state when unpatched
description: J1/J4/J7/J10 tip normals are open. Their Sallen-Key networks have only capacitors to ground and the high-impedance OPA4197 input; the ADC is isolated behind a follower. There is no passive DC return for an unpatched input. Leakage/initial charge therefore sets its voltage, and an unused input can generate arbitrary CV/gate/trigger readings.
recommendation: Ground only the fixed input jack normals. Keep bidirectional CTRL and OUT normals open, and update the all-jack-normal assertion accordingly. Open CTRL inputs also need an explicit firmware policy; their ADC input is not a zero-volt pull-down.
